claims.title: Common physical geometry
claims.assessment: With actual W held fixed, V=W-mu2*delta^2 is identical, so the prescribed center interval, feasibility, centers, weights and denominator are common at every allowed (delta,W).
claims.promotion_ceiling: Only the prescribed common-profile center-mixture family; no profile-specific support change.

claims.title: Uniform C3 averaged-kernel cancellation
claims.assessment: The Taylor integral remainder is bounded uniformly by the modulus of continuity of k''' on the compact support. Equal moments through degree3 cancel the polynomial and give o(delta^3), including atomic measures.
claims.promotion_ceiling: Right physical widths and a symbolic remainder bound; no evaluated numerical modulus or valid width.

claims.title: Common response derivatives through degree3
claims.assessment: The displayed moving-center chain rule retains u^3+3*u*mu2, 3*u*v and t terms. All total-order-at-most3 response partials depend on the common moments and common geometry.
claims.promotion_ceiling: An individual cubic coefficient need not vanish; W derivatives use actual variance.

claims.title: Actual one-sided simple-root regularity
claims.assessment: The divided-difference expression gives positive F_W from strict convexity. A compact local rectangle, IVT and monotonicity establish the unique nearby physical root; the right-derivative induction and integral remainder establish actual right-C3/C4 regularity.
claims.promotion_ceiling: Exact interior same-level premise and C>0; no negative-width continuation, boundary theorem or numerical zero-root enclosure.

claims.title: Common cubic root coefficient
claims.assessment: The third implicit derivative includes the required 3 and 6 multiplicities. Common response partials and simple-root regularity give common c,d,b3 and o(delta^3) separation.
claims.promotion_ceiling: No physical b3 value or new k''' component is evaluated.

claims.title: C4 response coefficient
claims.assessment: Uniform C4 remainder and identical finite-width geometry leave Delta_mu4 times the zero-width weighted k4 average divided by24. Other fourth-total-order partial differences vanish.
claims.promotion_ceiling: C4 is an additional regularity assumption; k''>0 and k'''<0 alone do not imply the value or sign of k4.

claims.title: Quartic root-transfer formula
claims.assessment: The mean-value identity transfers the response difference with factor -1/C. The ordinary coefficient is D4=-Delta_mu4*H4/(24*C); the first actual nonzero order is four when Delta_mu4*H4 is nonzero.
claims.promotion_ceiling: A zero D4 gives only o(delta^4); no finite-width equality or automatic later order.

claims.title: Same nonzero A normalization
claims.assessment: G=N-AQ has G_W=N_W-A=Q*C at the exact same-level reference. Common AQ cancels from a profile difference but A remains in the quotient denominator.
claims.promotion_ceiling: Stored finite-arithmetic A is retained; exact-real level identities do not certify a serialized root.

claims.title: Positive absolutely continuous profile pair
claims.assessment: The completed-square identity proves h_p>=2/7; direct polynomial antiderivatives give mass1, symmetry, mu2=1/3 and Delta_mu4=8/315 against uniform.
claims.promotion_ceiling: Continuous on [-1,1]; zero extensions jump at endpoints. The pair has the same full support.

claims.title: Pair-specific quartic coefficient
claims.assessment: Substituting Delta_mu4=8/315 into the root-transfer formula gives D4=-H4/(945*C).
claims.promotion_ceiling: Conditional exact same-level model formula; finite numerical substitution is a separate evidence class.

claims.title: Two-threshold gap coefficient
claims.assessment: Subtracting the two branch-specific root differences yields -Delta_mu4/24*(H4_0/C_0-H4_star/C_star).
claims.promotion_ceiling: Each branch retains its own A across profiles; no equality of branch levels or universal gap sign.

claims.title: C3 sharpness counterexample
claims.assessment: For 3<p<4 the endpoint power kernel remains C3, convex and negative in its third derivative under the stated parameter bounds. The positive Rodrigues-integral coefficient at the active endpoint gives a nonzero delta^p root separation; the interior contribution is O(delta^4).
claims.promotion_ceiling: A function-class counterexample, not a change to the frozen physical kernel or a numerical experiment.

claims.title: Degenerate cases and theorem boundaries
claims.assessment: Equal fourth moments or zero H4 erase the quartic term. Symmetric measures with mu2=0 or1 are unique; C=0 or a boundary reference invalidates the simple interior-root hypothesis.
claims.promotion_ceiling: No universal next order follows from a vanishing quartic coefficient.

claims.title: Fifth-order separation after quartic degeneracy
claims.assessment: The polynomial perturbation has H4=360*gamma*(V-w); the exact response difference is 15*gamma*Delta_mu4*(V-w)*delta^4+gamma*Delta_mu6*delta^6. Nonzero common c persists for small gamma, yielding the stated nonzero delta^5 root separation.
claims.promotion_ceiling: Smooth explicit counterexample only; no physical fifth-derivative or fifth-order coefficient campaign.
